land.text: the Obotrite lands between the Elbe and the Baltic, under Hermann Billung's march

successors.note: Drawing end only. The Billung March (936) put the tribes under German rule and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany shape covers Mecklenburg from 947, but the Obotrite principality lasted to 1167 (page) and rose against the Germans in 983.

capitals.name: Veligard (Mecklenburg, Michelenburg)
capitals.note: The infobox gives the capital as 'Veligard or Veligrad (German: Michelenburg)' with no dates; the trading port Reric appears on the page only as an emporium.

keyframe_review.note: 11,729 km2, 793-805 (47 cells: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 34, Schleswig-Holstein 10, Brandenburg 2). The Obotrites page gives 'Formed: 8th century', Witzlaus as first ruler (to about 795) and, from the Bavarian Geographer of 830, '53 civitates'; no area and no boundary, so no infobox comparison was possible. The Obotrites were 'allies of Charlemagne for decades' (undated).

New keyframe, 804-805: Cliopatria adds the Holstein land (19 cells, 14 of them in Schleswig-Holstein) in 806, two years after the page: 'The part of their former land in Holstein north of Elbe was awarded to the Obotrites in 804, as a reward for their victory.'

correction.text: the Obotrites with Holstein north of the Elbe, awarded by Charlemagne in 804

keyframe_review.note: 15,439 km2, 806-813, right for 804-813. The Danish king Gudfred struck the Obotrites 'in their former Saxon lands' in 808, destroyed Reric and drove Drozko from his land, who came back in 809 with Saxon auxiliaries; Gudfred was murdered in 810. The Obotrites page says a Danish invasion 'soon reversed' the grant, but the Nordalbingia page has the Danes pushed back across the Eider in 808, and the land stays Obotrite until 814 (next shape).

15,291 km2, 814-881: Cliopatria keeps the Holstein cells although the Nordalbingia page says 'After Charlemagne's death in 814, the Nordalbingian Saxons were pardoned and their land restored to them from the Obotrites'. The 19-cell addition of 806 is in the shape (806 minus 814 is zero cells); removing its 14 Schleswig-Holstein cells restores the 793 outline in Holstein (the five Mecklenburg cells stay).

correction.text: the Obotrite lands without the Holstein cells awarded in 804 and restored to the Nordalbingian Saxons in 814

keyframe_review.note: 15,114 km2, 882-883: one cell less; the page gives nothing for the ninth-century frontier. Louis the German forced the Obotrites to accept his authority in 844 and sent Louis the Younger against the Abodrite, Linone and Sorb tribes in 858 (Louis the German page); no land changed hands on the page.
15,200 km2, 884-886: one cell more than 882; nothing on the page.
15,291 km2, 887-935: the 814 outline; the page has nothing for 887-935 and the Danish wars (808-1200) moved no border it dates.

15,116 km2, 936-946: one cell less. The Billung March page: formed in 936 when Otto 'made Hermann Billung princeps militiae'; Hermann was 'granted control of the border with rule over the West Slavic Obotrite tribes, including the Polabians, Warnabi and Wagri'. The tribes keep their own princes (Nako is named in 955), so the shape is kept, as a German-ruled land.

ledger.note: 793: the Obotrites enter the record as a confederation of Polabian Slav tribes on the Baltic coast. The Obotrites page gives 'Formed: 8th century', a first ruler Witzlaus (died about 795) and no founding year; 793 is Cliopatria's first shape, so the year bridges a silence.

798: the Obotrites beat the Nordalbingian Saxons at Bornhoeved. 'The Obotrites under Prince Thrasco defeated the Saxons in the Battle of Bornhoeved (798).' The Nordalbingia page has the Franks and their Obotrite allies led by Prince Drozko (name differs); 'The areas north of the Elbe were at first given to the Obotrites'.

region.text: Nordalbingia, the Saxon land north of the Elbe (Holstein)

ledger.note: 804: the fighting for Nordalbingia ends with Charlemagne's award. 'In 804, as a reward for their victory' (Obotrites page).

804: Charlemagne awards Holstein to the Obotrites. Former Saxon land in Holstein north of the Elbe was awarded to the Obotrites 'in 804, as a reward for their victory'. The region is Cliopatria's 14 Schleswig-Holstein cells of the 806 addition.

808: Gudfred of Denmark strikes the Obotrites. He 'struck the Obotrites in their former Saxon lands by sea', destroyed 'Reric by the Baltic coast' and drove Drozko from his land; the Slavic lands accepted Danish overlordship. The Nordalbingia page: Charles the Younger 'pushed them back across the Eider River' in 808. The counterpart is Cliopatria's Scandinavian minor kingdoms row, which covers the Danes.

region.text: the Obotrite lands: Holstein and the Baltic coast with Reric

ledger.note: 810: Gudfred is murdered by one of his housecarls and the Danish pressure ends. Drozko had returned in 809 with Saxon auxiliaries and 'reasserted control over the Slavic lands that had accepted Danish overlordship' before being murdered himself in the rebuilt Reric; Gudfred's successor Hemming made peace with the Franks in 811; the page does not mention the Obotrites in connection with that peace.

814: Charlemagne's death returns Nordalbingia to the Saxons. 'After Charlemagne's death in 814, the Nordalbingian Saxons were pardoned and their land restored to them from the Obotrites.' The Saxon state had ended in 804 (saxons dossier); the land passes to the Frankish crown's Nordalbingian Saxons.

region.text: the Nordalbingian land north of the Elbe

ledger.note: 946: the Obotrites leave the map. Cliopatria's row ends in 946 and its Kingdom of Germany covers Mecklenburg from 947; the pages date no end of the Obotrites then. The Billung March page: formed in 936 with 'rule over the West Slavic Obotrite tribes'; 'in 955 the Obotrite chief Nako' revolted and was 'completely defeated' on the Recknitz; the march was abandoned after the Obotrite and Veleti rising of 983; the Obotrites page ends the princely line in 1167.

wars.name: Saxon Wars (Obotrite share)
wars.outcome: The Obotrites, Charlemagne's allies, beat the Nordalbingian Saxons at Bornhoeved (798); the Saxon land in Holstein north of the Elbe was awarded to them in 804, and 'The areas north of the Elbe were at first given to the Obotrites' (Nordalbingia page); in 814 it went back to the Saxons.
wars.note: The Obotrites page names Prince Thrasco; the Nordalbingia page Prince Drozko; the Gudfred page has Drozko (Thrasco) driven out in 808 and murdered in 809, the Obotrites page lists Thrasco as ruler to about 810.

wars.name: Danish war of Gudfred against the Obotrites
wars.outcome: Gudfred destroyed Reric and subjected the Slav lands in 808; Drozko returned in 809 with Saxon auxiliaries, attacked the Wilzi and recovered the lands; Gudfred was murdered in 810.
wars.note: The Obotrites page dates the Danish wars 'from 808 to 1200'.

wars.name: East Frankish campaign against the Abodrites, Linones and Sorbs
wars.outcome: Louis the Younger and Thachulf were sent against the tribes in 858; the page gives no result. In 844 Louis the German had forced the Obotrites 'to accept his authority' (east-franks ledger, vassal).
wars.note: No border moved on the page.

wars.name: Billung March wars
wars.outcome: Hermann Billung was given rule over the Obotrite tribes in 936; in 955 the Obotrite chief Nako rose with Hermann's nephews and was completely defeated on the Recknitz by King Otto.
wars.note: The Obotrites page calls the same battle 'Raxa'. The march was abandoned after the 983 rising.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the Obotrite lands: the Elbe against the Saxons, the Baltic coast and the Slav frontiers are approximate. The Holstein addition (804-814) is named only as 'north of the Elbe'.

notes: Obotrites (eu-07-d), four pages of the five budgeted (Obotrites, Billung March, Nordalbingia, Gudfred) plus Louis the German, opened under the East Francia budget and reused for 844 and 858. No page gives an area or a boundary. Cliopatria rows. (1) The Holstein grant of 804 is drawn in 806 (new keyframe obotrites_804) and never taken back; the Nordalbingia page restores it to the Saxons in 814 (verdict adjust). The 19-cell addition is the whole difference between the 793 and 806 shapes, 14 of them in Schleswig-Holstein. (2) The row ends in 946, 221 years before the page's last Obotrite prince (1167); the dissolve event in 946 is a drawing end at confidence 1, not a political end. The Obotrites were Hermann Billung's subjects from 936 (page) and a recurring enemy to 983 and beyond; a later group should decide whether to extend the dossier or leave Mecklenburg to the Kingdom of Germany. Not settled. The pages disagree on the leader at Bornhoeved (Thrasco, Obotrites page; Drozko, Nordalbingia page) and on Drozko's end (driven out 808 and murdered 809 on the Gudfred page; the Obotrites page has Thrasco ruling to about 810). The Obotrites page says the Danes 'soon reversed' the 804 award; the Nordalbingia page says the Danes were pushed back across the Eider in 808. No ruler list is given (the page's succession table is partial), so no rulers are recorded. The East Frankish vassalage of 844 (Louis the German page) is in the east-franks dossier; the Obotrite side has no event type for it. No page here dates the Obotrites 826-935 except those. Counterparts: saxons (dossier ends 804), kingdom-of-the-franks, scandinavian-minor-kingdoms (eu-14), kingdom-of-germany (eu-08). Gazetteer: all names used resolve.
